text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Endangered species law soon: Protections are 'important aspect of biodiversity conservation,' Prime Minister Jean Chretien says.
- Dole ready to play rough: Election battle could get nasty.
- Prime Minister's brother may testify at Krever blood inquiry: Ontario plans to use Michel Chretien in defence of policy.
- 58 names gives race for mayor circus air: Barb E. Doll in Vancouver bid.
- New Northwest Territories constitution would reserve native seats: 1999 division of territories will alter racial balance.
- Texan eager to buy Prairie branch lines: Founder of RailTex Inc in the market for grain-carrying branch lines on the Prairies that the major railways want to abandon.
- Dow Jones breaks 6,000: Surging oil stocks propel blue-chip index decisively above milestone.
- RailTex shops in Canada: The entrepreneurial Texas railway is trying to diversify by adding Prairie grain-carrying branch lines to its fast-growing portfolio.
- Former Canadian prime minister Brian Mulroney praised for Archer-Daniels-Midland Co deal: Analysts say he brokered fair settlement of price-fixing case.
- Data defects haunt Ontario Pension Board: Numerous errors in membership information could affect thousands.
- Cameco in C$105-million coup: Uranium giant swoops for North American interests of Britain's Magnox, strengthens foothold in U.S. and gains access to key low-cost mining technology.

- Cam-Net stung while chasing share price deals: Communications company was pursuing at least two major deals tied to its share price during March, the same month the FBI alleges CEO was bribing brokers to artificially boost the price of Cam-Net stock.
